task.description: Re-implement Letflow.Engine.Transition.collect_leaf_gateways/3 from scratch per iteration 3 of lib/letflow/design/iss0398-walk-to-gateway-fix.md (now CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS after two rounds of rework) -- replacing the prior exponential-blowup implementation with a memoized Tarjan-SCC single-pass DFS (index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index bundled in a leaf_search_state()), correcting the memo-key-unsoundness BLOCKER the validator found in the plain node-keyed scheme (memo value for a node on a cycle depended on which cycle member was entered first). find_matching_join/2 rewritten to thread the whole leaf_search_state() across sibling branches (memo survives, index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index reset per branch).
acceptance_criteria: collect_leaf_gateways/3 (arity 3, not iteration 2's /4) implements design doc §2.2.2's exact five-step algorithm: memo hit, on-stack (empty-set contribution), node-lookup-fails terminal, PARALLEL_GATEWAY immediate terminal (never pushed onto stack), and the branching-node explore/fold/SCC-closure-check step
SCC closure (§2.2.2's closure check, local_lowlink == index[node_id]) writes one shared aggregate leaf value to memo for every popped SCC member
find_matching_join/2 threads leaf_search_state() across sibling branches per §2.5: memo carried forward, index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index reset to empty/0 between branches
PARALLEL_GATEWAY-immediate-terminal rule (§2.3) preserved exactly, short-circuited before any stack push
AC1-AC6 (three_branch_graph/0) and the iteration-1 ISS-0398 fixtures (branch_with_exclusive_gateway_graph/0, ambiguous_branch_dead_ends_graph/0) pass unchanged

New fixtures added per §4: diamond_chain_graph/1 (parameterized stress fixture, run at a k large enough to genuinely demonstrate the fix), cyclic_escape_graph/0 + cyclic_escape_graph_reversed_edges/0 (asserting identical results across both edge orders), pure_cycle_no_escape_graph/0 (empty-aggregate case)
mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix letflow.check.test run to completion with real quoted output

result.summary:
Replaced the iteration-1/2 collect_leaf_gateways implementation in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex in place with the design's SCC-aware algorithm: added leaf_search_state()/leaf_search_result() @type declarations, fresh_leaf_search_state/0, reset_stack_bookkeeping/1, put_leaf_memo/3, and split the traversal into collect_leaf_gateways/3 (steps 1-4: memo hit, on-stack empty-set contribution, unresolved-node terminal, PARALLEL_GATEWAY immediate terminal -- never pushed onto stack, so it can never be pulled into an SCC), explore_branching_node/3 (step 5's index/lowlink assignment and stack push), fold_outgoing_edges/4 (the sequential state-threaded fold over outgoing edges, unioning leaves and folding min(lowlink)), and close_scc_or_defer/5 (the closure check: local_lowlink == own_index pops the stack down through and including node_id and writes the SAME local_leaves aggregate to memo for every popped member; otherwise returns {:open, local_lowlink} leaving the node on stack). find_matching_join/2's outer Enum.reduce_while now threads {:ok, acc_join_id, state} instead of {:ok, acc_join_id}, calling reset_stack_bookkeeping/1 before each branch's collect_leaf_gateways/3 call so memo survives across branches while index/lowlink/stack/stack_set/next_index reset to empty/0, matching §2.5 exactly. The private moduledoc comment above collect_leaf_gateways/3 was rewritten to describe the memoized-Tarjan-SCC-DFS behavior (order-independence via SCC-closure, not per-node memoization) rather than iteration 1/2's stale description.

Added to test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs: diamond_chain_graph/1 (a 2-outgoing-edge split -- branch 0 is the zero-hop control branch straight to "join" so gateway_role/2 classifies "split" as a real :split (out-degree > 1), branch 1 is a parameterized chain of k EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY diamonds reconverging on "join"), run at k=40 (nodes/edges = 123/162, comfortably inside @max_nodes 500/@max_edges 2000) with a wall-clock assertion under a 2-second budget -- actual measured time was 6.9ms for k=40 (O(2^40) ~= 10^12 calls under the old unmemoized scheme would never complete in any practical time; this revision's O(nodes+edges) scheme is essentially instant). cyclic_escape_graph/0 and cyclic_escape_graph_reversed_edges/0 (the exact X->GW->C->B(->GW cycles, ->D escapes)->JOIN counterexample from design doc §2.4b, with the split's edges_out order swapped in the twin) -- both fixtures assert full-result-tuple-equivalent outcomes (both resolve to {:ok, ..., [{:parallel_split, ...}]} with 2 branch_ids and a JoinCounter on the real "JOIN" node), confirming order-independence holds in practice, not just in the design's own hand-trace. pure_cycle_no_escape_graph/0 (a 2-node A<->B escape-less cycle, split given 2 duplicate edges into the cycle so it classifies as a real :split) asserts {:error, {:no_matching_join_found, "split"}} -- the empty-aggregate case.

Of the 15 full-suite failures, 14 are pre-existing environmental/order-dependent flakiness entirely unrelated to this change (Letflow.TenantSchemaReaperTest concurrent-invocation liveness x2, Letflow.Scheduler.PollerTest AC5 retention-guard timing x2, Letflow.ServiceCatalogTest AC6/AC7 referential-guard tests x5, Letflow.SandboxPoolTest provisioning-mailbox timing, Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest rust-pin tests x2) -- confirmed by re-running exactly those 5 test files in isolation immediately afterward: all 62 tests passed cleanly (mix test test/letflow/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs test/mix/tasks/letflow/check_toolchain_test.exs -> "Finished in 43.1 seconds ... Result: 62 passed"), proving these are full-suite-load/timing artifacts (DB schema-drop races, wall-clock-budget assertions under contention, rust-toolchain-check races), not regressions from this commit.

The 15th failure IS caused by this change and is EXPECTED, not a defect: Letflow.SchedulerReq188Test "lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex has zero diff against the base branch" (test/letflow/scheduler_req188_test.exs:432) literally asserts `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex` is empty. This guard was written when REQ-188 shipped to confirm THAT requirement didn't touch transition.ex, but it is written as a permanent "zero diff against main forever" assertion rather than being scoped to REQ-188's own commit range -- it was ALREADY broken on this branch before this rework, by iteration 1's own commit 5691a6a2 ("fix(ISS-0398): broaden walk_to_gateway into collect_leaf_gateways..."), which already touched transition.ex; confirmed via `git log --oneline -- lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex` showing 5691a6a2 predates this rework's own commit. Re-ran test/letflow/engine/ plus this one test file together in isolation to confirm it is the ONLY real failure and everything else in the engine suite is green: "Finished in 120.8 seconds ... Result: 905/906 passed (1/1 property, 904/905 tests), 7 excluded, Failed: 1 test" (the transition.ex-diff guard). Flagging for REVIEWER: this test's premise (any future legitimate change to transition.ex will always fail it) is now structurally obsolete given ISS-0398's whole purpose is exactly such a change; recommend either scoping it to a specific historical commit range or retiring it, but that edit is TEST-DESIGNER/test-file territory, not something ELIXIR-DEV silently changed here.
